newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia says hopes to join CEFTA in near future.
newsitem.headline: Croatia says hopes to join CEFTA in near future.

text.p: Croatia's Prime Minister Zlatko Matesa said on Thursday his country hoped to join the Central European trade integration soon after reaching bilateral accords with some CEFTA members.

"We are negotiating on free trade zones with Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary and hope that we can reach bilateral agreement at the beginning of next year," Matesa told an international conference on investment.
Following its admission to the Council of Europe on Wednesday, he said one of Croatia's strategic goals in the near future was to resume negotiations on trade and cooperation with the European Union.

Matesa said Croatia with its low inflation rate and budget deficit met nearly all of the Maastricht criteria but had to further lower interest rates, which have fallen to 20 percent from over 30 percent so far this year.
Most of the country's exports, totalling $3.2 billion in the first nine months this year, were to the EU and Italy and Germany topped the list of its foreign trade partners.

But talks on stronger ties with Europe that would pave the way for a preferential treatment in trade, and funds from the so-called PHARE programme of support to post-communist reforms, were suspended almost two years ago. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
